title: Teardown button on case-study pages
hypothesis: Because the inne case study has no teardown button and the only exit is 'Back to Home', we believe adding the button after the summary and at the end will raise teardown clicks from readers of the case study, for visitors who reach it from the home page.
metric: cal.com link clicks from case-study pages
steps: Add header button, mid-page button and closing block
decide: Keep if clicks from case-study pages rise above the before-period; the read is directional, not proof.

title: Contact page becomes a booking page
hypothesis: Because Contact lists four equal options and no booking link, we believe putting the teardown button first will move enquiries from email to booking, for visitors who open Contact.
metric: cal.com clicks from the contact page vs emails received
steps: Rewrite H1 and put the button first
decide: Keep if booking clicks from Contact rise and enquiries do not fall overall.

title: Measure the booking click
hypothesis: Because no event fires on the cal.com links, we believe adding one will give a real baseline and show which pages produce teardown requests, for the owner.
metric: cta_click events per page and per month
steps: Add the event to every cal.com link
Test-click each link and confirm it arrives
Request cal.com export to confirm bookings
decide: Done when each link produces an event; replace the assumed baseline with measured numbers.

title: Explain the teardown and who it is for
hypothesis: Because P2 did not know what a 'teardown' is or whether the service fits DTC brands, we believe a one-line explanation and a 'for ...' line will raise clicks, for first-time mobile visitors.
metric: Do 5 target buyers say what the teardown is and who it is for, unprompted?
steps: Show 5 target buyers the current hero and ask
decide: Keep the new copy if at least 4 of 5 describe it correctly.
